draftNote: 1 of five queued off a bottom-two lane: Cuban Noobster (jungle→carry).

coaching.headline: Zero fights won to their five — four of those cashed — is how four paper-favored lanes turned into a 0-6 tower loss in 25 minutes.
coaching.team: The paper gave us four of five lanes (carry, mid, jungle, support all favored) and the early game backed it up: Xeebs opened with first blood on Kallari at 2.3, and at 10 Crunch and Scarlett traded 1-for-1 deep in their half while the first Fangtooth fell to us at 11 — a real cross-map trade and the best macro of the game. It unraveled on numbers, not matchups. The 0-2 at 14.6 in their half was taken while support, jungle and carry were all elsewhere; the 1-2 at their Fangtooth at 16.9 was a two-man fight against three with Countess and Drongo alive, ahead in lane, and absent — and Fangtooth fell at 17.6. From 19 on every fight was at their towers and lost: 2-4 at 19 pricing the outer at 19.6 and inner at 20.1, three of ours dying 0-3 to just Sparrow and Renna at 21.3 pricing Fangtooth at 22.6, and 1-4 at 23.4. The line to remember is the 23-minute Fangtooth: all five of us alive and it fell uncontested — that is a map-awareness problem, not a numbers problem. Next game: nobody starts a fight near a major until mid and carry have shoved and started walking.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What was the plan at their Fangtooth at 16.9? Kwang and Scarlett took a two-man fight into three while Countess and Drongo — both alive and ahead in lane — never left their lanes. It went 1-2, Fangtooth fell at 17.6, and the 19-minute teamfight that followed at their outer tower went 2-4 with the deaths pricing three towers (19.6, 20.1, 20.8). That stretch turned an even Fangtooth ledger into their game.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's cross-map read at 10 was right — trading 1-for-1 deep in their half while the 11-minute Fangtooth was banked. The rest of the map went the other way: alive but never joining the 0-2 at 14.6, and deaths that kept getting priced — the 10.2 death ahead of the outer tower at 11.6, the 17.1 death ahead of Fangtooth at 17.6, the 21.5 death ahead of Fangtooth at 22.6. Jungle is tempo: when a fight starts near a major, Scarlett arriving is worth more than any camp.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim won the lane on paper, but the map never saw the lead: alive and ahead while the 0-2 at 14.6 and the 1-2 at their Fangtooth (16.9) were being lost. The 19 death priced the outer at 19.6 and inner at 20.1, and the 21.3 death priced Fangtooth at 22.6. Two completed items in 25 minutes with Tainted Rounds — the third piece of the 58.1% Lightning Hawk/Vanquisher/Tainted Rounds core — never built meant the late fights ran without the win condition online.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs took first blood on Kallari at 2.3 and killed Murdock again at 10 in the Fangtooth trade — then gave it back one pick at a time: caught alone by Murdock at 6.9, 13.1 and 18, with only 2 wards placed all game and no armor bought into a three-physical comp. A dead offlaner opens the river, and the river went 16 buffs to our 6.

7682f9ea-ae1d-42fe-adf4-89bf55b76e97.text: Countess held the one mid matchup the paper called ours all game and returned 0/3/0 with zero objective damage and no rotation to the Fangtooth fight next door at 16.9 — a won lane left in the lane.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.text: Kwang did the support job — 12 wards, the 8.1 kill on Riktor deep in our jungle, and a body in nearly every fight; six deaths is the price of being the only one who kept showing up.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.text: Every one of Scarlett's four deaths was followed by a falling tower or Fangtooth (11.6, 17.6, 22.6, 24.5) — the jungle's deaths were the most expensive on the team.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Ahead in lane and absent from both mid-game fights that decided the map — the 0-2 at 14.6 and the 1-2 at their Fangtooth at 16.9 — a carry lead that never leaves the lane is a lead the team never had.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: First blood at 2.3, then three solo deaths to the same Murdock (6.9, 13.1, 18) on 2 wards — the one lane the paper called unfavored, and it was donated in the fog.

coaching.whatWorked: The 10-minute trade deep in their half — Crunch and Scarlett committing across the map while the first Fangtooth fell at 11 — was the one true cross-map play of the game. Bodies spent where the objective was the prize: that read held up and is the piece to keep.

23.4.call: What changed since the 19-minute loss at their outer tower to make a third try at the same walls the right call? Nothing had — after two collapses on that ground, the play was to stop knocking, set up at our own structures, and make them start the next fight into us.

19.call: With Fangtooth just lost at 17.6, what did a five-man engage at their outer tower win even if it went perfectly? The reset was the play — group on our own side, hold for the next spawn, and take the fight where their walk is the long one.

21.3.call: Why trade at their outer tower with a Fangtooth spawn live on the map? The objective was the prize of that window, and it was standing across the map while three committed to the walls — the play was to set up on the spawn with vision and let them start the fight into us.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Kallari. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s), Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s), Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
